samples.text:
The graph shows the average number of people who used bus, metro and tram every day in a European city from 2010 to 2022.

In 2010, the metro was the most popular with 610 thousand passengers per day, and the bus had 520 thousand. The tram was much less popular, it had only 90 thousand passengers. After that the metro increased every year and reached 820 thousand in 2018. On the other hand, the number of bus passenger went down slowly to 430 thousand in 2018. The tram also grew and it was 210 thousand in 2018.

In 2020 all three types of transport had a big fall. The metro dropped to 470 thousand, the bus to 260 thousand and the tram to 130 thousand. In 2022 the numbers went up again. The metro was 790 thousand, the bus was 380 thousand and tram was 225 thousand, which was it's highest number.

Overall, the metro was the most used transport and the tram was the least used. Bus decreased but metro and tram increased in the period.
samples.why: Overview placed at the end and somewhat basic · key features including the 2020 fall covered · repetitive structures · comma splice, article and agreement errors that do not obscure meaning.

samples.text:
The line graph compares the average daily number of passengers travelling by bus, metro and tram in a European city between 2010 and 2022.

Overall, the metro carried the most passengers throughout the period, and its use grew considerably, as did that of the tram. Bus usage, however, declined. All three modes saw a sharp fall in 2020, followed by a partial recovery.

In 2010, around 610,000 people used the metro each day, compared with 520,000 bus passengers and just 90,000 tram users. Over the next eight years, metro ridership rose steadily to 820,000, while the tram more than doubled to 210,000. Bus numbers, in contrast, was falling gradually to 430,000 in 2018.

The year 2020 marked a dramatic drop for every mode. The metro fell to 470,000 passengers a day, the bus to 260,000 and the tram to 130,000. By 2022, the figures had largely bounced back: the metro recovered to 790,000, slightly below its earlier peak, and the bus rose to 380,000. The tram, meanwhile, reached 225,000, the highest figure for this mode over the whole period.
samples.why: Clear overview covering growth, decline and the 2020 fall · logical paragraphing · good range of linking · appropriate vocabulary such as 'ridership' · mostly error-free with one minor slip.

samples.text:
The graph illustrates how many passengers, on average, used the bus, metro and tram networks each day in a European city over a twelve-year period beginning in 2010.

The metro was consistently the busiest mode of public transport, and both it and the tram became more heavily used over time, whereas bus travel gradually lost popularity. A further notable feature is the abrupt slump in all three services in 2020, from which they had mostly recovered by 2022.

At the outset, the metro carried 610,000 passengers daily, ahead of the bus with 520,000, while the tram lagged far behind at 90,000. Between 2010 and 2018, the metro gained steadily, peaking at 820,000, and tram use rose to 210,000, more than twice its initial level. Bus journeys moved in the opposite direction, easing down to 430,000.

In 2020, passenger numbers plummeted across the board, with the metro falling to 470,000, the bus to 260,000 and the tram to 130,000. The subsequent rebound was strong but uneven: by 2022 the metro had almost returned to its peak at 790,000, and the tram actually hit a new high of 225,000, yet bus usage, at 380,000, remained well below its 2010 figure.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected, including the uneven recovery · overview clear and well placed · figures accurate and used for comparison · precise, varied vocabulary · wide range of error-free structures.
